## Benchmark DNA public scorecard

1. Credit scoring and risk — CONFORMS
2. Evidence-integrity anomaly detection — CONFORMS
3. Trading and portfolio decisions — CONFORMS
4. Robo-advice — CONFORMS
5. Payments and money movement — CONFORMS
6. Chatbots as product — CONFORMS
7. Pinned terminology — CONFORMS
8. Deterministic and reproducible checks — CONFORMS
9. Fail-closed export — GAP. Implement a pinned export gate and record its acceptance and rejection checks.
10. Consent before capture — CONFORMS
11. Human-readable boundary receipt — CONFORMS
12. Per-record verdicts — CONFORMS
13. Bias and exclusion — GAP. Obtain independent bias testing on a stated dataset.
14. Privacy and data protection — GAP. Obtain an independent privacy evaluation of capture, storage and export.
15. Vendor integration risk — CONFORMS
16. Deterministic high-assurance checks — CONFORMS
17. Security assurance — GAP. Complete an independent examination and obtain its issued report. The file records a quote only.
18. Scope of standards and regulatory claims — CONFORMS
19. Open banking interface boundary — CONFORMS
20. Institutional systems boundary — CONFORMS
21. RegTech evidence workflow — CONFORMS
22. Community evidence and fiscal sponsorship — CONFORMS
23. Measured savings boundary — CONFORMS
24. Fiscal-sponsorship execution — GAP. Obtain the signed agreement and sponsor IRS letter.

## Handshake Profile – official TXT





Network Working Group                                           V. Jones
Internet-Draft                                     Entercation Info Inc.
Intended status: Informational                          24 November 2026
Expires: 28 May 2027


 Cryptographic Handshake Profile for Fiscal-Sponsorship Onboarding and
                         Outer Pilot Execution
                  draft-jones-outerprise-handshake-01

Abstract

   This individual Internet-Draft proposes a detached evidence exchange
   for sponsor onboarding, a bounded pilot, and an institutional review.
   A synthetic trace specifies byte-level commitments and evidence
   links.  The profile concerns evidence handling and leaves funding,
   institutional decisions, and legal eligibility to the responsible
   parties.

Status of This Memo

   This Internet-Draft is submitted in full conformance with the
   provisions of BCP 78 and BCP 79.

   Internet-Drafts are working documents of the Internet Engineering
   Task Force (IETF).  Note that other groups may also distribute
   working documents as Internet-Drafts.  The list of current Internet-
   Drafts is at https://datatracker.ietf.org/drafts/current/.

   Internet-Drafts are draft documents valid for a maximum of six months
   and may be updated, replaced, or obsoleted by other documents at any
   time.  It is inappropriate to use Internet-Drafts as reference
   material or to cite them other than as "work in progress."

   This Internet-Draft will expire on 28 May 2027.

Copyright Notice

   Copyright (c) 2026 IETF Trust and the persons identified as the
   document authors.  All rights reserved.

1.  Scope and Ontology

   The proposed application role is evidence generation and delivery.
   Credit scoring, model training, credit decisions, institutional API
   integration and payment execution are outside scope.  The walkthrough
   is synthetic.  AI 2030 is a proposed demonstration partner and all
   fixture identities, decisions and payments are fictional.  No
   participation, adoption or endorsement is implied.  Current
   deployment of the proposed wire format is UNVERIFIED.

   Issuer  An actor that makes and signs a scoped Statement under an
      assigned role.

   Recipient  An actor that receives an identified package and may
      separately acknowledge receipt, verify it, or issue a disposition
      under its authority.

   Transparency Service  A service accepting and registering Signed



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 2]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


      Statements in the architecture of [RFC9943].  Registration is
      optional and outside the local synthetic trace.

   Statement  A typed assertion about an identified project and event.

   Receipt  In SCITT usage, applicable service-issued proof evidence
      using [RFC9942] and a specified verifiable data structure profile.
      This draft's sponsor decision, policy evaluation and recipient
      acknowledgment are application Statements.  They are COSE signed
      objects when signed using this profile.

   Pair Key  A public-format relationship tag derived from identifiers.
      It supplies neither identity verification nor access control.

   Transaction Attestation Ledger (TAL)  A sequence of linked project
      records documenting observed workflow events.  A presented tip
      binds a particular predecessor chain.

   Outer Pilot  A bounded execution of one charter, from intake to
      reviewed handoff.

   Four Gates  Validation establishes documentary readiness.  Trust
      records the intended pairing and role approvals.  Engagement runs
      the agreed workflow.  Procurement records a separate buying
      decision where authorized.

   Workflow context and optional demonstration: Entercation application
   (https://entercation.lovable.app/).  The link is informative and may
   evolve.

2.  Encoding and Cryptographic Operations

   Use RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 for JSON objects, with duplicate names
   rejected before canonicalization.  This profile uses strings for
   numeric quantities and timestamps.  Digests are SHA-256 and
   transported as exactly 64 lowercase ASCII hexadecimal characters.
   H(label, bytes) is SHA-256 of the ASCII prefix outerprise-handshake/
   v1/, the ASCII label, a single zero octet, and the supplied bytes in
   that order.  Use raw SHA-256 over file octets for manifest entries
   and file references.  The domain-separated hashes in this profile are
   separate from file hashes.

   For signed objects, encode a tagged COSE_Sign1 (tag 18) with an
   embedded JCS payload, an empty unprotected map, and a 64-byte Ed25519
   signature.  For this synthetic profile the protected header is
   deterministic CBOR {1: -19, 4: kid} with a one-octet byte-string kid,
   encoded in that key order.  The signature input is the deterministic
   CBOR encoding of ["Signature1", protected-header byte string, empty



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 3]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


   byte string, payload byte string].  Use Ed25519 as defined in RFC
   8032, without prehashing.  Use the verifier's separately configured
   trusted role-to-key mapping.  The kid is a lookup hint.  See
   [RFC8949], [RFC9052], [RFC9053] and [RFC9864], [RFC8032] and
   [RFC8785].

3.  The Cryptographic Handshake Sequence

3.1.  Gate 1: Validation

   The sponsor presents the determination letter, EIN, applicable UEI
   and SAM evidence, and a versioned management AI RMF self-map.  The
   project operator presents the Founder Portfolio.  Record a project
   ID, policy version and event time.  The intake object has keys
   artifacts, policy, project, time, sponsor_ein, project_ein, and uei.
   Artifacts maps filenames to raw file digest hex.  Compute H("intake",
   JCS(intake)).  Source authority and applicability are reviewed
   separately.  See Section 5.

3.2.  Gate 2: Trust

   After documentary identity checks, encode each EIN as nine ASCII
   digits, preserving leading zeroes and omitting punctuation.  Compute
   H("sponsor-ein", sponsor digits) and H("project-ein", project
   digits).  Concatenate the two lowercase digest hex strings in sponsor
   then project order, yielding exactly 128 ASCII characters.  Scope all
   evidence to the separate project ID and policy.  The same entity pair
   can operate multiple projects.  The Pair Key is predictable from its
   inputs and can correlate projects.  Apply disclosure controls to the
   identifiers and tag.

3.3.  Gate 3: Engagement

   The positive TAL trace is Submitted, Decided, Disbursed, Confirmed,
   and EOT written.  Every record has keys intake, pair_key, policy,
   previous, project, state, and time.  The initial previous is 64 ASCII
   zeroes.  Each later previous is the predecessor's H("tal",
   JCS(record)).  Require matching project, policy, intake and pair
   across the trace.  This funding trace proceeds through Disbursed only
   with separately authorized disbursement evidence.  A decline or
   missing evidence halts this positive trace.

   At Decided, the sponsor signs the TAL base fields plus outcome.  The
   validator signs an object with decision (raw file digest of the
   complete decision COSE object), policy, project, result, and time.
   The Decided TAL record adds decision and evaluation, each the raw
   file digest of the corresponding complete COSE file.  Require issuer
   authority, validated signatures, and the expected scoped approve/pass



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 4]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


   outcomes before continuation.  Disbursed and Confirmed each add an
   evidence key naming the raw file digest of the relevant source
   specimen.  The EOT written record links to the Confirmed record
   through its predecessor digest.  EOT means Evidence of Transaction.
   The signed manifest authenticates the presented tip under the
   publisher role.  These fixtures model events rather than authorize
   movement of funds.  See the related Dual-Receipt Internet-Draft
   (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-jones-scitt-dual-receipt/)
   for a separately specified profile.

3.4.  Observation Scope and Chain Findings

   Report the result for the records presented for the expected project,
   policy, intake, and Pair Key. The manifest tip identifies the tip of
   the presented chain.  A consistent chain establishes the topology of
   those records.  Completeness, global uniqueness, and freshness
   require separate evidence.  Use separate findings for signature
   verification, stream binding, and decision-maker authority.

   For topology reporting, deduplicate exact repeated records by their
   H("tal", JCS(record)) digest.  Report CONFLICT if the presented
   stream includes competing authenticated roots or two distinct
   authenticated successors naming the same predecessor.  If no such
   conflict is established, report UNRESOLVED when a predecessor is
   missing, the chain is cyclic or disconnected, or the authenticated
   binding needed to classify the chain cannot be established.  Do not
   select a branch by timestamp.  Authentication of a record for this
   finding requires evidence binding its exact bytes to the expected
   stream.  Report the authority of the decision-maker separately.
   These findings do not replace the positive trace checks in
   Section 3.3.

3.5.  Decision Identity and Evaluation Binding

   In this profile, an evaluation binds to the complete tagged decision
   COSE_Sign1 object as delivered.  The verifier computes SHA-256 over
   all of its file octets, with no decoding, reserialization, or added
   prefix.  It compares the lowercase hexadecimal result with the signed
   evaluation's decision field.  A mismatch fails the exact-object
   binding check.  Verify the sponsor and validator signatures and their
   authority for the applicable scope separately.

   A stable payload identifier, if used by a companion system, is a
   correlation reference under that system's named identifier profile.
   A correlation match supplies no evidence that a particular signature,
   envelope, registration, or evaluation matches.  A service-local entry
   handle is a locator.  Registration evidence is assessed separately
   under the applicable transparency profile.



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 5]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


   When re-encapsulation changes the decision octets, preserve the
   original signed decision and its evaluation as the evidence for the
   earlier check.  To associate that evidence with another
   representation, an external procedure would need to verify the
   original exact-file binding and both original signatures,
   authenticate the relevant signer and role, establish payload
   equivalence, document the named transformation and verify its link
   between the two objects, and establish that the policy, scope, and
   all other inputs material to the evaluation remain applicable.  A new
   signed representation requires its own signature and authority
   checks.  This profile defines no transformation evidence format or
   substitution rule.  An evaluation of different decision octets with a
   valid exact-object binding requires a new signed evaluation of those
   octets.

3.6.  Gate 4: Procurement Evidence Package

   Build a JCS manifest with keys files, intake, policy, project,
   recipient, tal_tip, and time.  The files array is ordered by ASCII
   pathname, each entry having path, sha256, and size as a canonical
   decimal string.  Paths are unique single-component ASCII names using
   letters, digits, hyphen, underscore or period.  Reject dot and
   double-dot names, path collisions, extra files in the evidence
   payload, incorrect byte lengths and digest mismatches.  The manifest
   and its signed envelope are carried alongside the listed payload
   files.  Compute H("manifest", manifest bytes) and sign the same
   manifest bytes with the publisher role.  Provide the TAL records
   alongside the payload and verify their tip against the signed
   manifest.  The Macro is the handoff package.  Delivery,
   acknowledgment, verification and institutional disposition are
   separate events.  Sponsorship, participation in a specific grant and
   procurement are separate decisions, each made by the authority for
   that decision.  A separate institutional disposition identifies the
   manifest and the scope of a reviewer decision.  Procurement requires
   its own authorized agreement.

4.  Mathematical Determinism

   The evaluation-file vector applies raw SHA-256 to the complete
   247-octet tagged evaluation.cose file.  The result is
   0f87ca2790f64a39a7f3da3f5f4002f1f731b78e300c3aa380275befd2dcb510.
   The Decided record evaluation field and the manifest entry for
   evaluation.cose both carry this digest.  The companion test-vector
   appendix records exact preimages, COSE signing inputs and outputs.
   The synthetic clock value is 2026-11-24T12:00:00Z, the policy
   identifier is demo-policy-1, and the project identifier is demo-1.
   This time is a fixture field.  The public test seeds are 32
   repetitions of 0x01, 0x02 and 0x03 for sponsor, validator and



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 6]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


   publisher, with kids 0x53, 0x56 and 0x50 respectively.  Production
   clocks, role keys, policy and format deployment are UNVERIFIED.
   Fixture keys are restricted to tests.

   Recompute JCS bytes and compare them to embedded payloads, recompute
   raw and domain-separated digest values, reconstruct and verify
   signature inputs with trusted keys, and replay predecessor and role
   bindings in the stated order.  Compare each result to the pinned
   fixture.  A digest can check bytes against a trusted reference.
   Signer authorization, ledger completeness, accurate source statements
   and current eligibility require separate evidence.

5.  Fiscal Sponsorship and the Federal Applicant Gate

   For a covered federal application, document the identity of the
   actual applicant, its UEI, and current SAM registration as required
   by the funding opportunity and applicable provisions of [PART25],
   including applicable exceptions.  Record source, retrieval time,
   status, expiry where available, and the verified binding of UEI to
   the applicant.  A UEI alone does not establish active registration.
   Where a requirement is unresolved, report UNVERIFIED and withhold any
   readiness conclusion.  Keep determination letters and sponsor
   authority evidence under controlled access.

   AI 2030 Group Inc. and EIN 99-3038309 identify a prospective case
   from supplied records.  Its current SAM status and UEI are UNVERIFIED
   for this proposal.  The packet can document a source check where
   application instructions allow supporting material.  It supplies no
   SAM registration, eligibility decision, fiscal sponsorship agreement
   or finding of compliance.  The applicability of the federal gate
   depends on the relevant program and the party's actual role.

6.  Engagement and Acknowledgment Protocol

   Following author approval, the author may submit this individual
   draft to Datatracker and invite reviewers, including Tiara Martinez
   or a designated reviewer, to reproduce the public vectors.
   Participation is UNVERIFIED.  Record a successful reproduction
   against a pinned version and artifact digest.  An acknowledgment
   identifies reviewer, date, fixture IDs, observed digest or result,
   and the tested implementation.  A signature and authority policy are
   required for any acknowledgment used as authorized evidence.  Its
   encoding is outside this version's runnable profile.

   PROPOSED THRESHOLD — NOT YET MET: 89 independent verification runs
   are required by the proposed procurement policy for the label
   implementation-verified.  A run is a documented reproduction of the
   agreed suite by an independently controlled reviewer and



Jones                      Expires 28 May 2027                  [Page 7]

Internet-Draft            Outerprise Handshake             November 2026


   implementation.  Deduplicate identical runs and identify distinct
   people and implementations separately.  Repeated executions of this
   reference checker and checks on other drafts do not count.  The
   threshold is a proposed local policy and does not confer standards
   adoption, acceptance or approval.

7.  Laboratory and Governance Boundaries

   [HB15017] specifies accreditation requirements for cryptographic and
   security testing laboratories.  The Outerprise application holds no
   NVLAP accreditation, CAVP validation or CMVP certification.
   Laboratory validation of this implementation is UNVERIFIED.  A
   laboratory with the relevant scope could assess applicable algorithm
   or module test inputs under the governing program requirements.  Any
   resulting report would identify its own scope.  The [AIRMF] self-map
   is management evidence.  Relevant pointers include GOVERN 6.1 and
   MANAGE 3.1 for third-party controls, MAP 2.2 and MAP 4.1 for use
   limits and dependencies, and MEASURE 2.4 for production monitoring.
   This fixture establishes none of those operating outcomes.

8.  Security and Privacy Considerations

   Check project, artifact digest, intended recipient, expected role,
   applicable policy, and freshness before accepting a record for a new
   use.  A recipient should detect previously processed artifact
   identifiers and require separately authenticated disposition
   evidence.  Duplicate delivery must not create a new milestone.
   Section 3.4 defines the limits of the presented chain.  A timestamp
   field is a claim.  Optional RFC 3161 evidence has a separately
   assessed timestamp authority and message imprint.

   Deterministic EIN hashes are enumerable and linkable.  Treat the Pair
   Key as an internal correlation value and avoid public disclosure of
   real identifiers, testimony or sensitive records.  This version
   defines no salted commitment.  Any later commitment profile must
   specify domain, serialization, independent per-commitment randomness,
   secure opening custody, and disclosure scope.  Acknowledgment
   identifies delivery and institutional acceptance requires a separate
   decision.

9.  IANA Considerations

   This document requests no IANA actions.

## Pain Point Resolutions – official TXT





Network Working Group                                           V. Jones
Internet-Draft                                     Entercation Info Inc.
Intended status: Informational                          25 November 2026
Expires: 29 May 2027


   Resolution of SCITT and W3C Verification Ambiguities via Detached
                           Evidence Profiles
              draft-jones-scitt-pain-point-resolutions-00

Abstract

   RFC 9942 (COSE Receipts), RFC 9943 (the SCITT architecture), and the
   W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 provide the foundational
   architecture for transparent, verifiable statements.  Operational
   ambiguities remain in receipt verification, statement identity,
   status freshness, and the boundary between what a receipt proves and
   what a relying party must establish separately.  This document maps
   fifteen documented pain points to constructions in four individual
   Internet-Drafts (a dual-receipt profile, a detached evidence handoffs
   model, a reproducible-review method, and a handshake profile).  Where
   none of those drafts applies, it either proposes a construction or
   names the existing external mechanism, and for every pain point it
   states which case applies and what gap remains.  Delivery is
   detached: no API integration, standing connection, or middleware is
   required.  This document does not amend RFC 9942, RFC 9943, or any
   W3C Recommendation.  All test vectors are synthetic.

Status of This Memo

   This Internet-Draft is submitted in full conformance with the
   provisions of BCP 78 and BCP 79.

   Internet-Drafts are working documents of the Internet Engineering
   Task Force (IETF).  Note that other groups may also distribute
   working documents as Internet-Drafts.  The list of current Internet-
   Drafts is at https://datatracker.ietf.org/drafts/current/.

   Internet-Drafts are draft documents valid for a maximum of six months
   and may be updated, replaced, or obsoleted by other documents at any
   time.  It is inappropriate to use Internet-Drafts as reference
   material or to cite them other than as "work in progress."

   This Internet-Draft will expire on 29 May 2027.

1.  Introduction

   A claim about a receipt, a statement, or a decision is only as strong
   as the exact bytes a verifier can recompute, the exact signature it
   can check, and the exact boundary the evidence crossed.  Where a
   specification leaves a choice open (which bytes a leaf covers, which
   numbers a signature binds, which encoding a digest names), this
   document either cites a companion profile that pins the choice,
   proposes a pin, or states that it has none.  The author calls this
   byte-level discipline "bottomology"; the term carries no meaning
   beyond this sentence.

   Each pain point is analysed through four views:

   Ontological:
      Distinct acts are kept distinct.  An Acknowledgment records that a
      package was received and its bytes verified; an Approval records a
      decision under authority.  Registration records that a Signed
      Statement entered a log; it does not record that the statement is
      true.  A Receipt proves inclusion under a signed root; it does not
      prove truth, completeness, or freshness.

   Topological:
      Evidence crosses an institutional boundary only as a detached,
      self-contained package (a "Delivery Doc").  The recipient verifies
      it offline and records its own disposition as a separate
      statement.  No API, standing connection, or middleware is
      introduced.

   Cryptographic:
      The exact canonicalization, digest, tree, and signature
      construction, with a test vector where one exists.

   Navigational:
      The ordered recomputation path a verifier follows: for example,
      from a Receipt to the signed tree head, from the root to the leaf,
      from the leaf to the statement, and from a decision to the
      independent policy evaluation.  Earlier material by the author
      calls this path "algorithmic intellectual telemetry"; in this
      document the term means only that ordered recomputation path.

1.1.  Requirements Language

   The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
   "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and
   "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in
   BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all
   capitals, as shown here.



Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 3]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


1.2.  Terminology and Conventions

   JCS(v):  The JSON Canonicalization Scheme encoding [RFC8785] of v, as
      UTF-8 octets.  Inputs to JCS in this document MUST NOT contain
      duplicate member names.

   SHA-256(x):  SHA-256 over the octet string x, producing 32 octets.

   Hd(label, x):  SHA-256 over the ASCII octets "outerprise-resolutions/
      v1/", the ASCII label, one zero octet, and x, in that order.  Hd
      is used only for constructions this document proposes.  It is
      distinct from the plain H() of [JONES-DUAL-02]; where this
      document reproduces a construction of [JONES-DUAL-02], it uses
      that draft's plain SHA-256, unchanged.

   ||:  Octet concatenation.  A digest is carried as exactly 64
      lowercase hexadecimal characters representing 32 octets; every
      concatenation of digests in this document is over the 32-octet
      values, never over their hexadecimal text.

   The Coverage values used in Section 2 are:

   PROFILE:  the construction is defined in a cited companion draft.
   PROPOSED:  the construction is defined here for the first time and
      has no independent implementation.
   EXTERNAL:  an existing mechanism outside the companion drafts is
      named; this document adds no construction beyond what is stated.
   NONE:  no construction is offered.

1.3.  Relationship to Companion Drafts

   [JONES-DUAL-02] is a JSON profile.  It states that it does not use
   COSE, that its Receipt is not a COSE Receipt as defined in [RFC9942],
   and that it claims no conformance to [RFC9943] or [RFC9942].
   Constructions in this document that use COSE_Sign1 (Section 2.1 and
   vector V4 in Appendix A) are therefore new proposals, not
   restatements of [JONES-DUAL-02].

   [JONES-HANDOFFS-03] defines terminology and an architectural model
   and specifies no wire protocol.  [JONES-MIMS-01] is a review method.
   [JONES-HANDSHAKE-01] encodes numeric quantities as JSON strings,
   while [JONES-DUAL-02] and this document use JSON integers for tree
   size.  Appendix B lists the resulting alignment work.








Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 4]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026

   24 November 2026, which draws on the public record of the SCITT
   working group, [INTEROP], and the cited specifications.  "Spec
   status" gives the status of the underlying specification problem.
   "Coverage" (Section 1.2) gives what this document and its companions
   actually contribute.  Nothing in this section claims that an OPEN
   problem has been closed in the specifications where it was found.

    |     | deployment choice.        |             |                 |

    | E12 | Per-credential status     | PARTLY      | EXTERNAL        |
    |     | queries let an issuer     | ADDRESSED   |                 |
    |     | correlate holder, time,   |             |                 |
    |     | and verifier.             |             |                 |
    +-----+---------------------------+-------------+-----------------+
    | E13 | A bare presentation can   | PARTLY      | EXTERNAL;       |
    |     | be replayed to another    | ADDRESSED   | PROPOSED        |
    |     | verifier.                 |             | (binding value  |
    |     |                           |             | only)           |
    +-----+---------------------------+-------------+-----------------+
    | E14 | Verifiability does not    | OUT OF      | PROPOSED        |
    |     | imply truth; authority,   | SCOPE (data |                 |
    |     | binding, and policy fit   | model);     |                 |
    |     | are separate checks.      | OPEN        |                 |
    |     |                           | (ecosystem) |                 |
    +-----+---------------------------+-------------+-----------------+
    | E15 | RATS freshness and multi- | PARTLY      | EXTERNAL        |
    |     | evidence composition are  | ADDRESSED   |                 |
    |     | per-verifier policy.      |             |                 |
    +-----+---------------------------+-------------+-----------------+

                 Table 1: Pain Points, Status, and Coverage










Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 6]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


2.1.  E01: Receipt Position and Size

   In [RFC9942] signed inclusion proofs, the signature covers the Merkle
   root, while tree-size and leaf-index are carried in the unprotected
   header.  Errata 9316 and 9317 against [RFC9942] were reported on 18
   November 2026; their status has not been re-verified for this
   document.  A hackathon report at IETF 127 observed that one receipt
   was accepted for the issued (tree-size, leaf-index) pair and for 31
   other pairs among 8,255 edited pairs.  The errata note that, with
   tree-size held fixed, no other leaf-index verifies; the gap concerns
   position and size, not membership.

   [JONES-DUAL-02] Section 4.5 defines a JSON signed tree head (STH)
   signed directly with Ed25519.  This document proposes the same remedy
   carried in COSE: payload = JCS({"root": R, "tree_size": N}), where R
   is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters and N is a JSON integer,
   signed as a COSE_Sign1 [RFC9052] with protected header {1: -19}
   (Ed25519 [RFC8032] as registered by [RFC9864]) and an empty
   unprotected header.  The Sig_structure is ["Signature1", protected,
   h'', payload] per Section 4.4 of [RFC9052], in which "Signature1" is
   a CBOR text string.  A verifier relying on tree size MUST verify the
   STH first and MUST accept only if the recomputed root and the
   presented tree size both equal the signed values.

   The STH authenticates the root and the tree size.  It does not carry
   or authenticate the leaf index.  The leaf index is constrained only
   by recomputing the inclusion path under the signed tree size and
   rejecting any index not less than that size (Section 5.2 of
   [RFC9942]); this document relies on the errata observation above only
   as reported and does not claim that recomputation fixes the index in
   every case.  Neither [RFC9942] nor the V4 payload carries a normative
   log identifier, so a verified STH proves only that the holder of the
   verifying key signed that root and size.  The verifier MUST bind that
   key to the intended Transparency Service by means outside this
   document.

   Route:  Receipt, then STH, then root, then leaf.

   Vector:  V4 (Appendix A), including a negative control in which an
      edited tree_size fails verification.

   Boundary:  An unsigned tree size is never relied on; the leaf index
      is relied on only as constrained by recomputation under the signed
      size.

   Residual gap: this does not amend [RFC9942].  A stock [RFC9942]
   verifier that does not check an STH is unaffected by this document.




Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 7]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


2.2.  E02: Leaf Serialization

   Neither [RFC9943] nor [RFC9942] names the serialization of a log
   leaf.  This document proposes: SID = Hd("statement", JCS(stmt)); LEAF
   = Hd("leaf", SID); leaf hash = SHA-256(0x00 || LEAF); interior node =
   SHA-256(0x01 || left || right), following Section 2.1.1 of [RFC9162].

   Route:  Statement, then SID, then LEAF, under one rule.

   Vector:  V3 (Appendix A).

   Boundary:  Two verifiers applying this rule derive the same leaf;
      services that do not apply it are unaffected.

   Residual gap: this is a profile rule.  [JONES-DUAL-02] Section 5.4
   defines a different leaf (over the canonical form of the payload and
   its signature), so the companion drafts do not yet share one leaf
   rule (Appendix B, Issue 1).

2.3.  E03: Statement Identity

   The iss and sub claims group statements, and a SCRAPI locator is
   local to one service.  This document proposes SID = Hd("statement",
   JCS(stmt)) for JSON statements.  JCS removes member-order and
   whitespace freedom (vector V2).

   Route:  Any JSON spelling, then JCS, then SID.

   Vector:  V1 and V2 (Appendix A).

   Boundary:  References cite a SID rather than a service-local locator.

   Residual gap: JCS applies only to JSON.  It does not address CBOR re-
   encoding of COSE Signed Statements.  Reference format, matching rule,
   and relation vocabulary remain open; see
   [I-D.gruszka-scitt-statement-identification].

2.4.  E04: Registration Is Not Truth

   Section 9.2 of [RFC9943] states that registering a statement only
   proves it was produced by an Issuer and that Issuers can make false
   statements, and Section 9.3 of [RFC9943] notes that Issuers may
   register selectively.  An Issuer can supersede an earlier statement
   by registering a later Signed Statement (Section 9.2 of [RFC9943]),
   but no standard field links a later statement to the one it
   supersedes.  [VCDM2] Section 1.1 states: "Verifiability of a
   credential does not imply the truth of claims encoded therein."




Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 8]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


   This document reuses [JONES-DUAL-02] Sections 5.2 and 5.6 unchanged:
   D1 = SHA-256(canon(payload_A)), D2 = SHA-256(canon(payload_B)), and
   CID = SHA-256(D1 || D2) over 64 input octets, D1 first.

   Route:  Decision, then the independent policy evaluation.

   Vector:  V5 (Appendix A) recomputes the composite identifier
      published in [JONES-DUAL-02].

   Boundary:  Decision and evaluation are signed by different keys;
      neither is read as truth.

   Residual gap: separating who decided from who evaluated against a
   policy does not make either statement true, does not show that no
   conflicting evaluation exists, does not prove completeness, and does
   not identify which later statement supersedes an earlier one; that
   link depends on the relation vocabulary left open under E03.

2.5.  E05: Operator-Defined Policy

   This document proposes that each decision cite the SID of the policy
   and trust-anchor set under which it was made, so that a historical
   check can be reproduced from the logged policy.  Residual gap: no
   interoperable policy format exists, and the construction helps only
   if the policy itself was logged.

2.6.  E06: Hash-Only Statements

   The payload_location header (260) of [RFC9995] is an optional hint.
   Terminology follows [JONES-HANDOFFS-03].  This document proposes
   payload digest = Hd("payload", bytes) (vector V6) and a third
   verdict: if the preimage cannot be obtained, the result is
   UNAVAILABLE, neither pass nor fail.  Content the verifier has not
   hashed is never accepted as seen.  Residual gap: no mandatory
   retrieval mechanism exists.

2.7.  E07: Asynchronous Registration

   [JONES-HANDSHAKE-01] halts its positive trace on a decline or on
   missing evidence.  This document adds that an entry identifier is not
   a Receipt and that the export gate (Section 3) records no milestone
   without a signed Receipt and a verified STH.  Residual gap: no
   standard machine-readable "not yet witnessed" state exists.








Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                  [Page 9]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


2.8.  E08: CCF Data-Hash

   For COSE-carried statements, this document adopts the rule of
   [I-D.ietf-scitt-receipts-ccf-profile]: the digest covers the
   COSE_Sign1 bytes as registered, with tag 18 retained and an empty
   unprotected header.  No construction is added.

2.9.  E09: Joint Statements

   No construction is offered.  The entry definition for joint
   statements remains unsettled.

2.10.  E10: Implementer Disagreement

   [INTEROP] records verifiers that each passed their own tests yet
   disagreed with one another.  [JONES-MIMS-01] pins the revision, the
   digest of the acquired bytes, the extraction rule, dependency
   versions, one proposition, and the expected comparison, and records
   the observed result.  Vector V4 includes a negative control in which
   "Signature1" is encoded as a CBOR byte string: an implementation that
   verifies raw bytes without rebuilding the Sig_structure would not
   detect that error, which is itself an instance of E10.  Residual gap:
   the method detects disagreement; it does not repair specification
   text.

2.11.  E11: Status Freshness

   Status mechanisms exist in [BSL] and [I-D.ietf-oauth-status-list].
   This document proposes only that a verifier record the status-list
   fetch time and the maximum staleness it accepted, so that a result is
   never presented as current on the strength of a signature alone.

2.12.  E12: Status Correlation

   [BSL] requires an uncompressed bitstring of at least 16 KB (131,072
   entries) to provide group privacy, which is probabilistic.  No
   construction is added.

2.13.  E13: Replay

   External mechanisms include the Data Integrity challenge and domain
   properties, the key binding of [RFC9901] over nonce and audience, and
   [I-D.ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc].  This document proposes a binding value,
   binding = Hd("presentation", challenge || 0x00 || domain || 0x00 ||
   SID) (vector V7); the challenge and domain MUST NOT contain a zero
   octet.





Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                 [Page 10]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


   The binding value by itself proves nothing about who presented it and
   does not prevent replay.  It MUST be covered by a signature made with
   a key bound to the credential, for example the key binding of
   [RFC9901] or a Data Integrity proof, and the verifier MUST verify
   that signature and that the signing key is the key bound to the
   credential.  Replay resistance comes from the verifier: the challenge
   MUST be issued by the verifier, fresh, single-use, and time-limited,
   and the verifier MUST record each challenge it accepts and refuse its
   reuse.  Vector V7 tests only the binding value.

2.14.  E14: Verifiability Is Not Truth

   This document proposes that a decision record list five verdicts
   separately: (1) signature validity, (2) issuer authority, (3) subject
   binding, (4) status, and (5) claim evidence.  A missing verdict is a
   refusal, and no verdict is inferred from another.

2.15.  E15: RATS Freshness

   This is outside the scope of the companion drafts.  The nonce,
   timestamp, and counter mechanisms of [RFC9334] apply; this document
   adds nothing.

3.  The Fail-Closed Architecture

   The export gate is the single enforcement point for evidence
   integrity.  A package leaves the sender only when every applicable
   check has passed against pinned bytes: the STH verifies under a key
   bound to the intended Transparency Service; the leaf recomputes to
   the signed root; the SID matches the statement; the decision and the
   policy evaluation are both present, signed by different keys, and
   verified against keys bound to their roles; any claimed payload
   preimage has been obtained and hashed; and any presentation binding
   is signed and matches its challenge and domain.  Any failure, missing
   input, or unsigned number is a refusal to export, and a refused
   package produces no Decided, Disbursed, or Confirmed record.

   Passing the gate establishes only that the evidence is intact and
   correctly bound.  It is not authorization to act.  A package that
   passes may carry a verified decline: that is verified evidence of a
   negative decision and MUST NOT be treated as authorization.  An
   action record such as Disbursed additionally requires that the
   verified decision outcome is approve, that the policy evaluation
   result is pass, and that the signer of the decision holds authority
   for that action under the cited policy (Section 2.5).  Establishing
   that authority is outside this document.





Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                 [Page 11]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


   The gate is an architectural sketch.  This document does not define a
   gate input format, a key-to-role binding mechanism, or an outcome
   vocabulary, and no implementation is claimed.

   On the recipient side, a package that cannot be verified is not
   accepted.  The recipient's disposition (Acknowledgment or Approval)
   is a separate statement with its own SID and is never merged into the
   sender's evidence.  A local chain cannot rule out withheld records or
   conflicting views.

   With respect to E04, the gate never reads a receipt or a dual receipt
   as truth.  With respect to E10, every vector in Appendix A can be
   recomputed from this text alone, and a recomputation that disagrees
   is a finding against the text.

4.  Security Considerations

   Hash substitution:
      The constructions rely on the collision and second-preimage
      resistance of SHA-256.  Domain separation through the Hd labels
      prevents a digest computed in one context (statement, leaf,
      payload, presentation) from verifying in another.  The 0x00 and
      0x01 prefixes of [RFC9162] separate leaf hashes from interior
      hashes.

   Detached payload loss:
      A hash-only statement whose preimage is lost yields UNAVAILABLE,
      never a pass.  A party registering hash-only statements SHOULD
      retain or designate a retrieval path for as long as the statement
      is meant to be verifiable.

   Replay:
      A Receipt is bearer-like.  A replayed Receipt proves registration
      only and says nothing about the presenter.  Presentations are
      bound as described in Section 2.13.

   Key compromise:
      Revocation strategies are out of scope in [RFC9943] and here.  The
      test key in Appendix A is public and MUST NOT be used outside
      testing.

   Privacy:
      Deterministic digests of low-entropy identifiers are enumerable
      and linkable.  SIDs are correlation values, not identity
      verification or access control.  Real identifiers, testimony, and
      sensitive records MUST NOT be placed in statements registered on a
      public log.  No salted commitment is defined.




Jones                      Expires 29 May 2027                 [Page 12]

Internet-Draft        SCITT Pain-Point Resolutions         November 2026


   Time:
      Every timestamp is its signer's claim; registration time is the
      Transparency Service's claim.  [RFC3161] may supply independently
      evidenced time, which is assessed separately.

5.  IANA Considerations

   This document has no IANA actions.

Appendix A.  Test Vectors

   All vectors are synthetic.  They were generated by one reference
   script and regenerated three times with byte-identical output; the V4
   signature was also checked with a second Ed25519 implementation.
   That is one implementation by the author, not an independent
   verification.  Hexadecimal is lowercase.  The Ed25519 key below is
   published for testing only and MUST NOT be used for any other
   purpose.

   V1 (E03): statements i = 1 to 4 are the JSON objects below with "seq"
   set to i.  JCS(statement 1) is 99 octets: the members in the order
   shown, with no whitespace.

     { "iss": "demo-issuer-1", "seq": i,
       "statement": "demo-supply-chain-event",
       "sub": "demo-artifact-1", "v": 1 }

     SID[1] =
       d013c1539582b548b9a4488e7982bba73ee173ebfe49acab25c43a60fc6ff721
     SID[2] =
       0ef4b19432f8d5d26a5a3c3ee7544491c3863b8bca69be16feaef12bdaa9f620
     SID[3] =
       1f9f6458b72ddd84c0f4816a468674712a8cd56fe6224bbf437c337cf8a8ba25
     SID[4] =
       5a767c39168bd6dca4230b1316219b0ef1fe4e947f2452f8177f7887f22c2b23

   V2 (E03): statement 1 with its members in reverse order canonicalizes
   to the same JCS octets and therefore the same SID.

     SID =
       d013c1539582b548b9a4488e7982bba73ee173ebfe49acab25c43a60fc6ff721

   V3 (E02): leaves, leaf hashes, interior nodes, and root.

Appendix B.  Open Issues

   1.  Leaf rule alignment: [JONES-DUAL-02] Section 5.4 and Section 2.2
       define different leaves.  A later revision should adopt one rule
       for both or state which objects each rule applies to.

   2.  Number encoding: [JONES-HANDSHAKE-01] encodes numeric quantities
       as JSON strings, while [JONES-DUAL-02] and this document use JSON
       integers for tree size.

   3.  STH member set: the STH of [JONES-DUAL-02] Section 4.5 has the
       members typ, ts_key_id, tree_size, root, and
       registration_policy_sha256; V4 uses only root and tree_size.

   4.  CBOR identity: E03 remains open for COSE-encoded statements.

Appendix C.  What This Document Does Not Claim

   This is an individual Internet-Draft and a work in progress.  It has
   not been adopted by any working group and is not a standard.  It does
   not amend [RFC9942], [RFC9943], [RFC9162], or any W3C Recommendation,
   and it does not claim that any organization has implemented or
   endorsed it.  No independent verification of this document has been
   recorded; the 89-run threshold proposed in [JONES-HANDSHAKE-01] has
   not been met for this document.
